title: Solve it together: the cheapest ticket
idea: GUIDED PROBLEM via UEPCC. Choose and apply the MIN pattern to find the cheapest ticket.
problem: Ticket prices are [30, 18, 25, 22]. What is the cheapest ticket?

exercises.prompt:
PROBLEM: ticket prices [30, 18, 25, 22]. What is the cheapest?

Understand. What is the OUTPUT?
exercises.explanation: 'Cheapest' is the single smallest value — the min pattern. Name the output first.

exercises.prompt: How is this problem related to finding the LONGEST jump from the last lesson?
options: Same best-so-far pattern, but we replace when SMALLER (flip > to <)
exercises.explanation: Cheapest is min — the max pattern flipped. You already know the shape; you flip the comparison.

exercises.prompt: Example by hand. Scan [30, 18, 25, 22] keeping the smallest so far. What is the cheapest?
exercises.explanation: best drops 30 -> 18, and 25 and 22 never beat 18. The cheapest is 18 — your check value.

options: Min — keep a best-so-far, replace when smaller
exercises.explanation: 'Cheapest/smallest/lowest' is MIN: a best-so-far replaced on a smaller value.

blocks: Start best-so-far at the first price
For each price, if it is smaller, replace best
exercises.explanation: Start at the first price, replace on anything smaller, then show the smallest.

exercises.prompt: Code it. Arrange the lines to find the cheapest ticket.
exercises.explanation: Start best at the first price, loop, replace when smaller (<), print.
Replace best only when the price is smaller, so the sign is <.

exercises.prompt: Check. The code prints 18. Your hand example said 18. So...
options: It passes — output matches the example
exercises.explanation: Output matches the hand-found cheapest, so the min solution is correct.

exercises.prompt: New input: prices = [12, 12, 20]. With the same min code, what prints?
exercises.explanation: The cheapest is 12 (it appears twice). Min reports the single smallest value.

exercises.prompt: Starting best at 0 here would be wrong, because no positive price is smaller than 0.
exercises.explanation: best would stay 0 — a value not in the list. Starting at prices[0] is the safe habit for min.
